Hi Luca —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. To keep momentum and align with the MAP, I put together a concise sprint for the POC environment handoff and acceptance. High-level items: 

- Org setup: Redwood will provision a per-org service account and scope it to the POC project (read-only logs + inference write).
- API keys: we will generate two keys (staging + acceptance) and rotate once post-acceptance.
- IP allowlist: we need your egress IP ranges to open 10.0.40.0/24 and 10.0.41.0/24.
- VPC peering: propose a one-hour window for peering + smoke tests; expect a brief restart of our connectors.

Proposed dates (flexible):
- Org + service account created: Sep 16
- API keys issued & initial test: Sep 17
- IP allowlist validated & VPC peering window: Sep 18 (10:00–11:00 PT)
- Acceptance run & sign-off: Sep 22

Hannah, can you attach the environment spec and confirm the service account scopes and the peering steps?

Luca — if the dates look good, can you confirm the peering window and share the exact CIDR(s) you can open? If procurement needs a copy of the MAP or MSA, loop them in and I’ll share the DocuSign link.

Thanks,
Sofia Ivanova

Hi Luca —

Thanks for the quick reply. Short answers up front:
- Service account scopes: 
  * roles/logging.viewer (read-only)
  * roles/compute.networkViewer (to validate peering)
  * custom role: redwood.inference.invoke (minimal inference call permissions)

- API key behavior: staging keys are throttled in the platform by default (250 rps, soft cap) — we can set a stricter quota for the POC if you prefer. Acceptance key will have the normal MAP throughput.

I attached two things: poc_env_spec_v1.pdf (environment variables, endpoint URLs, example curl calls) and map_checkpoint_matrix.xlsx (milestone sign-off owners). A snippet from the spec is below for the peering step: 

--- start quoted spec ---
1) Create service account on CardioApps project: cardo-poc-sa@cardioapps.iam.gserviceaccount.com
2) Share public key for SSH tunnel if needed (we prefer mTLS but support SSH fallback)
3) Initiate peering from CardioApps side and share peering request ID with our infra console
4) Redwood accepts peering and we run connectivity smoke test (curl /health on inference endpoint)
--- end quoted spec ---

If you can share the peering request ID after initiation, I’ll keep our infra on standby to accept immediately within the 10:00–11:00 PT window.

— Hannah
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
